providers.name: REA Chrome DevTools Protocol observation provider

limitations: Artifact identity is unavailable for this observation.
Observation starts when REA attaches; prior network and console activity is unavailable.

Worker targets are a final inventory snapshot, not worker-session observation. Their attached flag describes any debugging client; this page-session collector does not observe worker network, console, or script events, and short-lived workers may be absent from the snapshot.

Raw network headers, bodies, cookies, storage values, console objects, and WebSocket payloads are never retained; explicitly requested primitive console text is retained verbatim, while payload captures retain value-free shapes.
Source maps are reported only as declarative URLs and are not fetched.
URL-less scripts and console events without an allowed source URL are excluded because their origin cannot be proven.
CDP discovery omitted the target attachment state; attached is reported as unknown.
Browser host platform and architecture were not observed.

provider.name: REA Chrome DevTools Protocol observation provider

limitations: Complete evidence is bounded by a 33554432-byte input budget, a 100663296-byte reply budget, and a 64-level nesting cap. Those have no runtime override. capture_timeout_ms is 30000 ms (omitted means 30000). HAR/SAZ/qlog use a 192 MiB Node old-generation heap (source default). The effective REA_CAPTURE_DECODER_OLD_GENERATION_MIB value is 192 MiB (source default; default 192 MiB, floor 8 MiB, maximum 16384 MiB). Set REA_CAPTURE_DECODER_OLD_GENERATION_MIB in the environment that starts REA to a decimal integer from 8 to 16384, then restart REA. In a running MCP server, use update_analysis_settings with setting capture.decoder_old_generation_mib and action set instead; the new value applies to new work without a REA restart. On Node.js the decoder passes --max-old-space-size=192 and removes inherited NODE_OPTIONS, so additional host memory and NODE_OPTIONS do not raise this heap. The 8 MiB semi-space stays fixed. On Bun the V8 flags are ignored. Windows limits the decoder's committed memory to this value plus a 512 MiB reserve. Other Bun hosts enforce no decoder heap limit. Mitmproxy decoding uses a 768 MiB Linux address-space limit.
Every record is decoded before selection; no partial success is returned on malformed input or a resource limit.
Grouping does not establish handler identity, URL-space schemas or causality.

Static decompiler observations do not establish runtime behavior; the APK is never executed.
Method signatures use provider display types; DEX prototypes come from frozen JADX metadata. Display names may be aliases, and overload indices are local to this engine and artifact.
Class inventories use parsed metadata before code generation, including synthetic members that may be omitted from decompiled source. Source positions remain unknown.

Incoming reference totals count JADX using nodes. Direct invoke entries within a using method report raw DEX code-unit offsets and method indexes, but coverage is limited to those nodes and directly matched invokes; it does not establish every possible dynamic or reflective call site.

Manifest summaries are parsed once by REA's bridge from the exact root AndroidManifest.xml resource, using namespace-aware XML attributes; decoded XML is retained. APK signatures, split APKs, native libraries and Android runtime capture are not verified by this provider.
